✅ Correct Answer: B — 1992 Hungarian Grand Prix

📖 Explanation:

The 1992 Hungarian Grand Prix marked the final time a pre-qualifying session was held in Formula 1. This system was used to weed out slower entrants when more than 30 cars were entered for a race weekend.

Following the Hungarian round, the Brabham team collapsed and withdrew from the championship, which automatically reduced the entry list to 30 cars.

This withdrawal eliminated the need for pre-qualifying starting from the next race in Belgium, and the rule was permanently discarded ahead of the 1993 season.
